PROJECT OVERVIEW

A privacy-first plagiarism detection platform designed for academic environments where data sovereignty is paramount. Unlike cloud-based solutions that upload documents to external servers, this system operates entirely on local infrastructure—keeping sensitive academic work within institutional boundaries.

The system uses ChromaDB for local vector storage and Ollama for on-device embeddings, enabling semantic similarity detection without internet connectivity. This makes it ideal for institutions with strict data privacy requirements or limited internet access.

Local Embeddings Pipeline

Ollama runs entirely on local hardware, converting documents to vector embeddings without cloud dependencies. Supports multiple embedding models including all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for fast processing and larger models for accuracy.

ChromaDB Vector Store

Documents are stored as vectors in local ChromaDB with metadata extraction. Supports cosine similarity search with configurable thresholds and filtered queries by document type or submission date.

Async Job Processing

SQLite-backed job queue ensures document processing survives application restarts. Background workers handle embedding generation, similarity calculation, and report generation without blocking the UI.

Semantic Understanding

Beyond string matching—detects paraphrased content, synonym substitution, and structural similarity through transformer-based embeddings that understand contextual meaning.
